text: [p.226] CHAPTER V PLASMAS IN MAGNETIC FIELDS 52. Permittivity of a collisionless cold plasma THIS chapter deals with the properties of plasmas in an external magnetic field, which are said to be magnetoactive. By forcing the charged particles to Illove in helical paths along the lines of force, the magnetic field exerts a profound influence on the behaviour of the plasma. In particular, it affects the dielectric properties. Let us first recall son-le general properties of the permittivity tensor in the presence of a magnetic field with induction B (see ECM, 582). As when the field is absent, equation (28.6) is valid: (52.1) According to Onsager's principle, this tensor is symmetrical when the signs of the field and the wave vector are simultaneously changed: ea (o, k; B) = qa(o, - k: - B). (52.2) If the medium is invariant under spatial inversion (as is an equilibrium plasma), the are even functions of k, and (52.2) becomes k; B) = ega(w, k; -B). (52.2a) It must be emphasized, however, that this property occurs only in a medium in thermodynamic equilibrium, unlike (52.1), which follows from the definition of ea . In the general case, the tensor may be divided into an Hermitian part 2(ea + < a) and an anti-Hermitian part 2(ea - eba). The latter determines the dissipation of the field energy in the medium; cf. (30.3). We shall begin the study of magnetoactive plasmas with the simple case of a "cold" collisionless plasma.
